chunks: And Abū Baṣīr said to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: A woman passes by a man, and he looks at her from behind.
He said: Would any of you be pleased that his family and his close female relatives be looked at?
I said: No. He said: Then approve for people what you approve for yourself.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman passing by in the scenario under discussion
key_terms.خَلْفِهَا: her back or behind; the direction of the man's gaze
key_terms.فَارْضَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا تَرْضَاهُ لِنَفْسِ: be pleased for others with what you are pleased with for yourself

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach about looking at a woman from behind as she passes?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that looking at women in a way one would dislike for one's own family is morally blameworthy. The Imam عليه السلام grounds the teaching in reciprocity: a believer should want for others what he wants for himself.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4972 - Abu Basir asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about a man who looks at a woman passing by and then turns to look at her from behind.
Imam (as) replied: "Would any of you like someone to look at his family or close female relatives?"

I said: "No."
Imam (as) said: "Then be pleased for others what you are pleased with for yourself."
